questions.q: Name two crops that the Harappan people grew for food.
questions.a: The Harappan people grew wheat and barley. A wrong answer here shows the student has not yet distinguished between early hunter-gatherers and the agricultural Harappan civilization.

questions.q: Why was the development of cotton cultivation significant for the Harappan people?
questions.a: It was significant because they were among the first people in the world to cultivate and weave cotton, showing they had advanced skills in clothing production. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks of the Harappans only as farmers and misses their role as innovators in textiles.

questions.q: If you were an archaeologist finding a piece of pottery with red slip and black designs, what would this tell you about the Harappan economy?
questions.a: It tells us that they had specialized craftspeople who didn't just make basic bowls, but decorated them, indicating a prosperous economy where people had time for art. A wrong answer reveals the student views these items as mere "trash" rather than evidence of economic specialization.

questions.q: How did keeping domestic animals like cattle and sheep help the Harappans survive alongside farming?
questions.a: Animals provided a steady source of food (milk/meat) and labor, acting as a "backup" or supplement when harvests were unpredictable. A wrong answer shows a misunderstanding of how a diverse economy provides more security than relying on crops alone.

questions.q: Is it accurate to say the Harappan economy was based *only* on farming? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, it is not accurate because they also relied on fishing, hunting, and highly developed crafts like pottery and bead-making to support their daily lives. A wrong answer indicates the student is ignoring the "craft" and "supplementary" aspects of their economy.

questions.q: If you had to design a "Harappan Daily Life" poster, which three items would you include to show they were prosperous?
questions.a: A student should choose items like a bag of wheat, a spindle for cotton, and a decorated pot. Poor answers that include modern items or items not mentioned (like iron tools) show a failure to apply historical context.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The Harappan economy was a thriving system based on agriculture, animal husbandry, and skilled ______ that allowed people to settle in large, organized cities.
Fill in the blank: Think about the lunchbox you bring to school today—does it have ______, vegetables, or perhaps something made of cotton?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to list at least three agricultural products of the Harappans and explain how their diverse economy (farming, animals, and crafts) supported a settled city life.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Think about the lunchbox you bring to school today—does it have grains, ______, or perhaps something made of cotton?
